q: Does the coherence-collapse-at-success-peak signature survive under realistic noise (dephasing T2, amplitude damping T1) at levels achievable on current NISQ hardware (IBM Quantum ~100 us T2, ion-trap ~1 s T2)?
basis: This replication used pure statevector simulation (no noise model). The paper's coherence-monotone framework is inherently sensitive to off-diagonal decay, so T2 dephasing should directly attack C_l1. The threshold at which the collapse signature becomes unresolvable is unknown from either the paper or this reproduction.
next_steps: Add qiskit_aer.noise.NoiseModel with parameterized T1, T2 depolarizing/dephasing on each gate; sweep T2 in [1 us, 1 ms] at n=5,6,7; recompute C_l1(k_peak)/C_l1(0) and identify the T2 threshold below which the collapse-ratio saturates (i.e., signature is lost). Compare threshold to superconducting vs ion-trap platform numbers.

q: Does the analog Grover algorithm (Farhi-Gutmann Hamiltonian H = E(|w><w| + |s><s|)) exhibit the same coherence-collapse-at-peak signature under continuous-time evolution, matched iteration-for-iteration to the discrete algorithm we reproduced?
basis: The paper is framed as the *discrete analogue of the analog* algorithm; this replication only ran the discrete side (Grover oracle + diffuser via Qiskit). The analog-discrete correspondence is asserted but not independently reproduced here.
next_steps: Implement Farhi-Gutmann H in QuTiP or scipy.linalg.expm; evolve rho(t) for t in [0, pi/E]; sample C_l1(t), C_r(t), P(t) at Trotter step matched to discrete k; overlay against discrete curves at n=3-5 to test whether the two collapse profiles coincide (as the paper claims) or diverge (a novel finding).

q: Does the coherence-collapse extend to structured search problems (Grover on satisfiability, unstructured DB with multiple marked items, amplitude-amplification variants) or is it specific to the single-marked-item textbook Grover?
basis: The paper only analyzes the canonical single-w Grover. Real quantum-speedup applications (Grover-for-SAT, quantum walk search on graphs) use amplitude amplification with different oracle structures, where the coherence signature may differ.
next_steps: Extend code/grover_coherence.py to (a) multiple-marked-items Grover (varying M in [1, N/4]); (b) fixed-point Grover (Yoder-Low-Chuang); (c) quantum-walk search on cycle/hypercube. Compare C_l1(k_peak)/C_l1(0) trajectory across variants; identify whether the collapse is universal or only single-w.

q: Could a hybrid analog-digital protocol (analog Hamiltonian evolution interleaved with discrete measurement / feedback) achieve better coherence retention while preserving the sqrt(N) speedup, i.e., is the coherence 'cost' of Grover fundamental or protocol-dependent?
basis: The paper treats coherence as a monotone consumed during search. If the consumption is protocol-specific (rather than a Landauer-like fundamental cost of amplitude amplification), hybrid protocols could outperform. The paper does not distinguish these cases.
next_steps: Design and simulate a scheduled-measurement Grover variant (weak measurement at k=k_opt/2 followed by conditional continuation); compare C_l1 trajectory vs pure-unitary Grover at matched final P. Also test analog H with time-dependent coupling E(t) (Roland-Cerf adiabatic Grover) and compare coherence trajectories to fixed-E analog and to discrete.

q: How does the coherence-collapse signature manifest on real analog-platform quantum simulators --- Rydberg-atom arrays with resonant global drive, trapped-ion Molmer-Sorensen-based amplitude amplification, or superconducting analog Grover on Google/IBM lattices --- and does the observed T2-dependent degradation match the theoretical noise model?
basis: This is the natural experimental test of the paper's picture. Rydberg-atom (Lukin group), trapped-ion (Monroe, Blatt), and superconducting (IBM, Google) platforms all support analog-Grover-style protocols but with different dominant decoherence channels. No public dataset was consulted or generated in this reproduction.
next_steps: (1) Search literature (Endres, Bernien 2017 Rydberg; Figgatt 2017 ion Grover) for published |psi(t)> tomography or purity/coherence data during Grover-style protocols; (2) if datasets exist, recompute C_l1(t) directly on the reconstructed rho(t) and compare to the noise-augmented simulation from question 1; (3) if none exist, draft a minimal experimental proposal (n=3 Rydberg atoms, 4-shot state tomography every 100 ns) that would produce the needed data.
